new_findings.claim: The T3-01 behaviour is correct, but four edge gaps remain.
new_findings.evidence: Probes: (a) a claim without author_attempt_id/author_execution_id, checked by the author's own attempt, reads ACCEPTED; (b) duplicate cure_id lines: one supersession whose old digest matches the last line retires an earlier stale line whose digest was never matched; (c) without --rulings a fabricated 'x_a9#e7 ruling ZZ9' passes, and 'test-adversarial#e1' matches as the substring 'adversarial#e1'; (d) output_sha256 'not-a-digest' counts as a machine result; (e) --rulings never checks that the named ruling concerns the retired cure id: the live supersession of EZEK-P0-CURE-toolkit-v2 cites #e2 R5, which ordered the retirement of the original toolkit claim, and it reads SUPERSEDED. No path reached ACCEPTED without the three-digest binding.
new_findings.suggested_fix: Refuse claims missing both author fields; refuse duplicate cure_ids, or match old digests per line; anchor the ORDERED_BY regex at a word boundary that excludes '-'; require --rulings on gating runs; validate digests as 64 hex characters; record in each supersession the ruling that names the retired cure id, or have the orchestrator log that link. Add vectors for each.

new_findings.claim: The paragraph_mark_claim, kq_claim and false_mark_absence_claim arms raise false positives on true disclosures (TQ-01..03), filling primaries' triage with noise.
